results.title: Contral: The agent which teaches while you build. | Product Hunt
results.content:
What works well is the contextual awareness. It picks up on what you are building and makes suggestions that fit the existing codebase rather than generating generic snippets you still have to rewrite anyway.

For anyone who does a lot of repetitive coding tasks or needs to ship quickly without a large team, this is a genuinely useful tool. It handles the boilerplate so you can focus on the logic that actually matters.

Still some rough edges in edge case handling, but the core experience is solid and the direction is right.

W

What do you think? …

Hey Product Hunt! I'm Devansh, co-founder of Contral.

Contral is out of beta today: Contral IDE 1.1 and the extension 1.0. [...] We started conversations with a few universities about running Contral as a pilot in their CS programs. The idea of students learning to code inside an actual IDE instead of switching between a tutorial and an editor resonated hard with the professors we spoke to. Nothing signed yet but the conversations are real and moving.

Bug reports have been humbling. Our early users don't hold back and thats exactly what we needed. We've shipped fixes almost daily since launch based on real user feedback. The product today is genuinely better than what we launched with a month ago.

4

9

Contral takes an interesting approach to AI-assisted coding. Rather than trying to replace the developer, it positions itself as a coding partner that helps you move faster without losing control of the output. [...] \- checks every turn. when the agent says "done!", contral compares what changed with what you asked for. it catches nothing changed, a missing function or file, a file that no longer parses, and placeholder code. smaller and free models get a specific correction automatically.

0

1

7mo ago

One month ago we launched Contral on Product Hunt and hit #1 Product of the Week. Here's what happened since.

500+ developers downloaded the beta. We didn't expect that number this early honestly. The feedback has been wild, some stuff we expected people to love (the teaching layer) and some stuff we didn't expect at all (Defense Mode became the most talked about feature by far, people genuinely love being quizzed on their own code which was surprising).

results.title: Claude Code Remote Control: Continue local sessions from any device with Remote Control | Product Hunt
results.content:
This is exactly what I always had in my bucket of TODOs, while I travel in bus to University and the way back is in total 3 hours and I believed having something like this would seriously make that time of mine productive.Been using the @Cursor Agents, @Jules and recently the @OpenClaw to work in that time of the day. This will be the next try but I always thought how about having a computer on the go with me in the bus (not literally but to be able to control one remotely). Visualising this I had one image like being able to project through maybe some VR glasses and do it? But to be cheap I also thought about how using a mobile maybe we can remotely do this and we're here.What you'll think about the future ? Let me know and I'll share something I truly believe is the future but so much [...] 630 followers

630 followers

I start a session at my desk and keep it going from my phone after I leave. That's the whole thing, and it just works. The mobile side is a lot better than I expected.

The session is stuck on whatever folder I launched it in. I want to switch the working directory from my phone, and reach files on my machine outside that folder.

It's first-party, so it talks to Claude directly. The other options I looked at were painful to set up, with extra user management and another app to wire in. Here I just use the Claude app I already have.

What do you think? …

Anthropic announced a new Claude Code feature called Remote Control. [...] The idea is pretty straightforward: you start a Claude Code session locally in your terminal, then continue them from your phone. Take a walk, see the sun, walk your dog without losing your flow. It's rolling out now to Max users as a research preview.

Anyone here on Max plan tried it yet? How the mobile experience feels in practice (latency, editing capabilities, etc.)?

Reminds me of @Macky which @sayuj\_suresh launched a few days ago. Inviting your thoughts on this launch Sayuj. :)

@rohanrecommends thanks for bringing up Macky! yesss this is a good product, but it allows access from mobile for already started sessions but Macky allows you to access your full terminal, so you can do all kinds of terminal stuff and not just Claude.
